questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have a british girlfriend studying in the UK, so It brought us closer for the term.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The classes was very well composed and really liked the way it was structured.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found it quite confusing at times, since you got so much information from different places. In the end it was all right but you had to keep a lot of attention in the process of applying for courses etc.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: not much really. Was in contact with people at the host university in case anything went wrong or I needed help but I kinda had to pursue it myself and was not greeted very well I would say.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: as mentioned above I did not receive much help I had to chase it.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: it was really difficult as a single semester student. the accommodation the university offered was so expensive and for most students not an option. I ended up being scammed for housing for around 10.000 dkk and would really have appreciated more information on risks and how to find accomodation so I would potentially have avoided being scammed.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: most first year students live on campus so if you are older you might want to find your own. but it is also easy to pick campus accommodation and guarantee to meet new people.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: very expensive and bad quality. A rip off.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: quite complicated but manageable. as long as you keep attention to what is going in and out of your email.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: you get contacted by the host university. then you apply for courses to be approved at your home university before applying for them at the host university. quite simple but a lot of back and forth and confusion.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: supervisors dedicated to exchange students.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: very. got the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: be prepared with what classes you want and get them approved quickly. I did not get my first ones so it caused a lot of stress.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: really liked it. small classes and a lot of discussion. forces the student to engage and prepare for classes bringing the combined participation of the classes to higher levels.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: they were good and accurate and the teachers helped a lot.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: in Manchester the classes were much smaller and intimate which suited my style of learning a lot. at my home university we have big lectures where you can kinda just zoom out and its quite hard to stay focused.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Thinking digital media
Big questions in the digital world
Races and technology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: the same as mine. they were really good and worked well together as a student studying media, IT and communication.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: as a dane most stuff is cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: loved the societies. I was in the climbing society and met a lot of people and had a great time outside of the academics.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: anything you can dream of really. any sport or hobby you can think of has a society and Manchester has quite a lot to offer in terms of sports, music and history.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: join a society. use the city and go explore the music culture.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: the city center and Chester outside of Manchester.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: very easy. been in the UK many times and they are not that different to danish people.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: join a society. and be prepared a big part of the culture involves going to the pub having a drink.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: it is very international and can be challenging to adjust to so many cultures at one time but also very enriching.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the pub, music and sports culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: be brave to do stuff. talk to people. find local spots and live like its your home.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: getting new friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: not feeling alone. found it quite difficult at times being far away from friends and family.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
